clue.text: Musician pockets article to cause confusion

indicators.note: to pocket something is to tuck it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Muddy Waters was the American blues singer and guitarist

explanation.surface: A performer slips some printed piece into a pocket to sow confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Muddy Waters was a Chicago blues giant, so 'Musician' must be read as his full name, split to hold the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddy the waters is an idiom for making a situation murkier and harder to understand.

clue.text: End of story after philosopher captured by rogue Roman general

indicators.note: after puts the story's last letter behind the rest
captured by means held inside, so the philosopher is held within the jumbled letters
rogue means wayward, so the letters of Roman go astray

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of story

explanation.surface: The end of the tale comes after a philosopher is caught by a wayward Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman general' looks like the definition, but Roman is the anagram fodder and general alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony was a Roman general, Caesar's ally and Cleopatra's lover.

clue.text: Dabbler in French says 'about the aunt'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around another

explanation.surface: An amateur linguist reports how to say 'about the aunt' in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French' governs all three words that follow, and 'about' is an instruction rather than part of the quoted phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is someone who dabbles in an art or subject without serious commitment, a synonym for dabbler.

clue.text: Inexperienced solver nibbling at the edges

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of nibbling

explanation.surface: A beginner at crosswords nibbles away cautiously at the outskirts of the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use solver for YOU, since the solver is the person reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people lack experience, so young serves as a synonym for inexperienced or green.

clue.text: Variety of game with mixed salad snack served in hotels

indicators.note: a dish served in something is placed inside it

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet; plural, so two of them

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tossed salad snack is on the menu in hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'hotels' supplies H twice, one at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack-and-slash is a genre of video game built around melee combat, so it is one kind of game.

clue.text: See 1
This shows heights change over time

indicators.note: over means covering, so one word spreads across the other

explanation.surface: A device that tracks how things alter as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change over time' looks like a phrase about gradual change; it is ALTER placed over TIME: AL-TIME-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is an instrument in aircraft that measures and displays altitude, that is, height.

clue.text: Still essentially hungry? Get service

indicators.note: the essence of a word is at its core, so only its central letters count

parts.note: the two central letters of hungry

explanation.surface: Still peckish? Then go and get served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a waiter after the question about hunger; it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so it is a kind of church service.

clue.text: See 7
Oddly out for free meal including a fresh start

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown out, leaving only the even ones

parts.note: second and fourth letters of free

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so one piece sits within another

explanation.surface: Someone strangely absent for a free lunch, which comes with a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes in right after the first letter of the meal, so the meal word becomes launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaunch is starting something such as a product or campaign again, which is a fresh start.

clue.text: Network's not OK, crashing all over the place

indicators.note: a crashing system falls apart, so its letters end up disordered
not here means without, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, with the s
these two letters are taken away

explanation.surface: The network isn't working, failing all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not OK' reads as 'unwell', but it is an instruction to drop the letters O and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strewn are scattered untidily, which is the same as being all over the place.

clue.text: In a cavalier fashion, occasionally admits what's written on political party ends

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of admits
a missive is a letter, something written

indicators.note: the ends of words are their final letters

parts.note: the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone casually concedes what has been written in a party's manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political party' looks like a source for a party abbreviation; only the last letter of each word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting dismissively means treating something as unworthy of attention, which is a cavalier, offhand manner.

clue.text: A shame swirling mist blurred vision

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of shame

indicators.note: something swirling is churned about, so these letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: It is a pity that swirling fog makes it hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Astigmatism is an eye defect from an irregularly curved cornea or lens, which causes blurred vision.

clue.text: Like kind blokes start to tolerate diversity

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Kindly men are beginning to accept variety.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a varied mixture of things, so it shows diversity.

clue.text: Reliance of French on money to cover study

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, enclosing it

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A French student relying on cash to fund study.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence are British pennies; den is a common crossword word for a study or private room.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependence and reliance are synonyms: both mean needing someone or something for support.

clue.text: Some evidence of contraception

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: five consecutive letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A sign that birth control was used.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a small mark or sign left behind, a bit of evidence that something happened.

clue.text: Help a mere wreck that won't live long

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, leaving these letters in disorder

explanation.surface: A plea to aid a mere wreck of a person who has not long to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral describes things that last only a short time, such as mayflies, so it fits short-lived.

clue.text: Returning brief essay, scheduled espresso cup

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the brief essay and scheduled are read right to left
brief means cut short, so the last letter of essay goes

explanation.surface: A short essay is sent back on schedule along with a coffee cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' covers both the trimmed essay and the word for scheduled, so the whole string is read backwards at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small coffee cup of the kind used for strong black coffee.

clue.text: Brazil coverage mad about energy company

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: Shell is a large oil and gas company

explanation.surface: Media reports from Brazil are furious about a fuel firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil coverage' reads as news from the country, but a brazil is a nut and its covering is a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazil nut is covered by a hard casing, so nutshells are literally a brazil's covering.

clue.text: Heron swimming in river

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so these letters move into another order

explanation.surface: A wading bird is paddling about in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Last of bottled cider items lost and sent to the wrong address

indicators.note: things lost have gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the remaining letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Bottles of cider went missing after a parcel was mailed to the wrong house.
explanation.definitionFit: Misdirected post has been routed to an incorrect destination, which is being sent to the wrong address.

clue.text: Police chief's left suffering with bug

indicators.note: in a bad way, so the remaining letters are jumbled
has gone away, so that letter is taken out
the chief of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of the police force has gone off sick with a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: POLICE loses its first letter P, and the remaining OLICE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium that can cause food poisoning, colloquially a bug.

clue.text: At heart not happy, sad Rolling Stone

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy member of the Rolling Stones, deep down unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' looks like the band; Rolling gives a letter and Stone alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone with shifting iridescent colours, so it is a kind of precious stone.

clue.text: Span location

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short stretch or period

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses: a brief stint, and a place where something is.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular place, and also a short stretch or spell, as in a spot of leave.

clue.text: Press ID

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press ID' looks like a journalist's card; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The papers are the newspapers collectively, and your papers are documents proving who you are.

clue.text: Musical venue after Spice Girl's instrument

indicators.note: after puts the venue behind the next piece in the order

parts.note: two of the Spice Girls were Mel B and Mel C
an odeon was an ancient Greek hall for musical performance, now a cinema name

explanation.surface: A concert hall stages a show following a Spice Girl's turn on her instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group; Odeon is also a familiar British cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodeon is a small accordion or reed organ, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Wee-wee one drop at a time?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: to urinate in a feeble trickle
setter's reading: wee doubled means small after small, gradually

explanation.walkthrough: Wee is Scottish for small, so 'wee-wee' is small and small again; the childish word for urinating supplies the drip-by-drip picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Little by little is an idiom meaning gradually, a bit at a time, like drops falling one by one.

clue.text: See 26
